newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta bounces back on mark as tensions ease.
newsitem.headline: Peseta bounces back on mark as tensions ease.

text.p: The peseta strengthened by midday on Monday, recovering from its initial weakness, as European markets overcame initial worries over EMU after the left's win in the French election on Sunday, dealers said.
A French socialist spokesman, backing a European Monetary and Economic Union with as many members as possible, was quoted by dealers as a factor offering support to the Spanish market.
"All European currencies recovered versus the mark. It seems, in the end, markets were excessively nervous ahead of the election," a dealer in Madrid said.
At 1120 GMT, the peseta was trading at 84.47/50 per mark while it opened at around 84.79/81.
A general recovery in French markets also helped support Spanish assets, dealers added.
